newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent diesel, unleaded diffs steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent diesel, unleaded diffs steady.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent diesel fuel and unleaded gasoline differentials were steady in quiet discussion late Tuesday, traders said.
The steady differentials left prices to track March heating oil and unleaded futures, which fell on the day in NYMEX trade on forecasts of warmer weather and seasonally weak gasoline demand.
Trade in the Midwest spot markets following the long holiday weekend, but buying interest was expected to continue supporting diesel and unleaded basis through the week, traders said.
"Basis should remain strong through the March expiry. After that, distillate should be steady but gasoline could go lower," one Group Three trader said early in the day.

Group Three and Chicago low sulphur diesel were at parity, talked 4.25/4.50 cents a gallon over NYMEX March heating oil for all February timings. High sulphur diesel was steady at 2.50/2.75 cents over the print in both markets, traders said.

Group Three unleaded remained 2.50/2.75 cents a gallon over NYMEX March unleaded, with premium talked 2.75 cents higher. Chicago unleaded was even with the print for February deliveries and bid 64 cents a gallon for March deliveries.

Jet/kero basis was steady after making a steady climb over the past two weeks as American Airlines and its pilots union squared off ahead of a strike deadline. A strike was averted late Friday when President Bill Clinton imposed a 60-day cooling off period.
